ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, DP is the tangent of the circle $\odot O$, with D being the point of tangency. The chord AB is parallel to DP. Extend BO to intersect $\odot O$ at point C and DP at point E. Extend AC to intersect DP at point F. Connect OD. AF is parallel to OD; If OD = 5 and AB = 8, find the length of the line segment EF.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given that OH $\perp$ AB, and AB = 8, \\
$\therefore$ BH = AH = 4, \\
$\therefore$ OH = $\sqrt{OB^{2} - BH^{2}}$ = $\sqrt{5^{2} - 4^{2}}$ = 3, \\
Given that BH $\parallel$ ED, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ BOH $\sim$ $\triangle$ EOD, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BH}{ED}$ = $\frac{OH}{OD}$, that is, $\frac{4}{ED}$ = $\frac{3}{5}$, \\
Solving this yields: ED = $\frac{20}{3}$, \\
Given that $\angle$BAC = $90^\circ$, DH $\perp$ AB, DH $\perp$ DP, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral AFDH is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ DF = AH = 4, \\
$\therefore$ EF = ED - DF = $\frac{20}{3} - 4$ = $\boxed{\frac{8}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the center O is inside the circle, D is the point of tangency of the circle and the lower horizontal straight line DP, and OD is drawn as a vertical radius; DP is the bottom horizontal tangent. The upper chord AB is drawn as a horizontal line, parallel to DP. The oblique line goes from B through O and C and is extended to E on the tangent. Another line goes from A through C and is extended to F on the tangent, and in the figure AF is parallel to OD, in a vertical direction. On the tangent, from left to right, E, F, D, P can be seen. Reasoning: Let H be the foot of the perpendicular from O to chord AB. The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, so AH=BH=AB/2=4. Because OB and OD are both radii of the circle, OB=OD=5, so in right triangle OBH, OH=sqrt(OB^2-BH^2)=sqrt(5^2-4^2)=3. Since AB∥DP, BH∥ED; also because H, O, D are collinear, OH and OD are collinear; and B, O, E are collinear. Therefore triangle BOH and triangle EOD are similar. Corresponding sides are proportional: BH/ED=OH/OD, that is 4/ED=3/5, solving gives ED=20/3. Also because B, O, C are collinear and O is the center of the circle, BC is a diameter, so the inscribed angle ∠BAC=90°. At the same time AF∥OD, OD is perpendicular to tangent DP, and AB∥DP, so AFDH forms a rectangle. Therefore DF=AH=4. In the figure E, F, D are on the same straight line, and F is between E and D, so EF=ED-DF=20/3-4=8/3.
